findings.description: The proposal details the export and import verification of run state via 'ci export-state' and 'ci import-state', but does not specify how the exported state archive is ingested or authenticated when transferred from a developer workstation to internal CI storage in the split cloud/CI execution model.
findings.subject: ci_adapter_jenkins_gitlab

findings.description: Native Windows and macOS platforms reject model-dispatching stages by design to uphold sandbox isolation, requiring developers on these platforms to install and maintain WSL2 or a Linux VM (Lima/UTM) with bwrap to run model stages.
findings.subject: os_portability_matrix

findings.description: The config TUI outputs proposals and diffs to '.runs/config-proposals/' and explicitly avoids executing git commands, necessitating manual human copying and committing into the repository policy tree under reviewed change.
findings.subject: config_tui

cost.evidence: Forbids paid API keys and usage-credit endpoints, relying on personal interactive developer CLI subscriptions for cloud design stages and local model runtimes for build stages.

maintainability.evidence: Zero third-party runtime dependencies using Python standard library only; uv tool packaging; configuration resolved from git trees at commit SHA; structured error taxonomy emitted as JSON lines.

reliability.evidence: State integrity is validated on import via sha256 manifests and hash chains; concurrency locks and idempotency keys (run_id, stage, input digest) prevent duplicate execution; expired state fails closed.

scalability.evidence: CI jobs are split and serialized per run ID using resource groups or Jenkins lock, though model execution remains constrained to bwrap-capable Linux hosts.

security.evidence: Confidential source tree and protected tests never reach cloud services; isolation probes verify mount, egress denial, and credential visibility per run; approvals require offline human signatures via ssh-keygen -Y bound to evidence digests.
